purpose: Ensures organization-wide policies and procedures for managing AI risk are documented, transparent, and actually implemented — not just aspirational.
summary: Policies, processes, procedures, and practices across the organization related to mapping, measuring, and managing AI risks are in place, transparent, and implemented effectively, including understanding legal and regulatory requirements, integrating trustworthy AI characteristics, and maintaining an inventory of AI systems.
expectedStatementElements: How legal and regulatory requirements involving AI are identified, tracked, and documented
How trustworthy AI characteristics (validity, safety, fairness, privacy, etc.) are reflected in organizational policy
How the organization determines the level of risk management activity appropriate to a given AI system
How AI systems across the organization are inventoried and tracked
How policies are reviewed and updated over time
evidenceExamples: Legal/regulatory requirement tracking log specific to AI
commonGaps: No central inventory of AI systems in use across the organization
AI policy exists but hasn't been reviewed since it was first written
No process tracks new AI-related legal or regulatory requirements as they emerge
Trustworthy AI characteristics aren't reflected in any concrete policy language
interviewQuestions: Do you have a current inventory of every AI system in use across the organization?
How do you track new AI-related laws or regulations that might apply to you?
When was your AI governance policy last reviewed or updated?
How does your policy define what 'trustworthy AI' means for your organization?
